name: Facet
text:
Do a single high-contrast dark theme with a manual one-click light toggle. This keeps the interface consistent and predictable, which sharpens visibility and liveliness in screencasts—dark mode reduces eye strain in low-light editing and makes data pop. The trade-off is that users who strongly prefer light mode must click to switch, but it avoids fragmenting the experience with auto-switching.

name: Pane
text: Pane: A one-click toggle still forces users to choose between modes—some will toggle back and forth, creating inconsistency in screencasts and training. A better alternative: default to a *single* high-contrast theme (dark or light) based on system preference, with a *persistent* user override stored in settings. Settle it by testing task completion speed and error rates in both themes with users who edit in mixed lighting.
